anomalies.observed: The regulator output is on +3.3V, while the local +3V3 net is separate. Neither net connects to the FCC or NAVC VDD pins: all listed VDD pins are unconnected; FCC VDDA and NAVC VSSA are also unconnected.
anomalies.expected: The specification says the 3.3 V rail supplies both MCUs. Their VDD pins must be connected to that rail, with the analog supply/ground pins connected appropriately.

evidence.quote: 3.3 V feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: The MCU core and I/O supplies are not connected to the regulator output in the design connectivity, so the processors cannot operate as intended. The distinct +3.3V and +3V3 nets also leave the apparent local rail disconnected from the regulated rail.

anomalies.observed: The FCC crystal nets connect to FCC1.5 (PE6) and FCC1.37 (PE7), not its PH0/PH1 oscillator pins. FCC1.12 (PH0) is only connected to C14, and FCC1.13 (PH1) is on the VREF+_FCC divider. The NAVC crystal and its associated nets have no connection to NAVC1; NAVC1.5/6 (PH0/PH1) only connect to capacitors.
anomalies.expected: Each specified 25 MHz HSE crystal should connect to its MCU's external oscillator input/output pins (PH0/PH1), with the associated load network.
anomalies.impact: Neither MCU has the specified crystal connected to its oscillator pins. The FCC crystal is routed to GPIO pins, while the NAVC crystal is isolated from the MCU; operation requiring the intended external clock may fail or use an unintended clock source.

parsed.summary: Anomalies are present: both MCUs' supply pins are left unconnected from the regulated 3.3 V rail, and neither 25 MHz crystal is correctly connected to its MCU oscillator pins. These connectivity faults prevent the board from behaving as specified.
